question: On how many language pairs do they show that preordering assisting language sentences helps translation quality?

evidence: We experimented with English INLINEFORM0 Hindi translation as the parent task. English is the assisting source language. Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Malayalam and Tamil are the primary source languages, and translation from these to Hindi constitute the child tasks. Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati and Marathi are Indo-Aryan languages, while Malayalam and Tamil are Dravidian languages. All these languages have a canonical SOV word order.

title: Addressing word-order Divergence in Multilingual Neural Machine Translation for extremely Low Resource Languages
answer_rationale: Text 10 (page=11, section=Results) explicitly states that experiments were conducted on the X-Hindi pair, where X is one of Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Tamil, and Malayalam — totaling five language pairs. Text 9 (page=1, section=Abstract) and Text 8 (page=10, section=Network) corroborate that these five languages were tested with pre-ordering to match SOV word order, showing significant improvements.
